study.question: Does the small benefit of auxiliary learning in shared user/context embeddings originate from positive-intent losses, negative losses, or their combination? Observed full-validation click AUC: DIN 0.6555440824; g3-r0022-selector_disabled and g3-r0024-context_all_control 0.6662458901; g3-r0024-context_none_control 0.6659481623, cart/fav-only 0.6662117095, buy-only 0.6661861763. Thus all-minus-none=0.0002977279 and the task-group interaction=all-cartfav-buy+none=-0.0002038333 at this one seed. Disabling whole task groups did not improve the parent, but loss-outcome origins were not tested. These are controlled single-seed observations, not evidence of statistical significance, measured gradient conflict, or repeated support. All-control click Logloss=0.1820521662 versus neither=0.1821305949; four-task mean AUC=0.8199631563 versus 0.8172696063. Validation auxiliary positives are cart 10428, fav 7717, buy 4036 of 2871767; actual training prevalence is unavailable here and is not invented.
study.hypothesis: Auxiliary positive losses may carry complementary preference information into shared context while negative-loss contributions dilute or interfere with it. Routing only positive auxiliary loss-to-context derivatives may retain the shared-context benefit and improve primary ranking relative to both-live or negative-only. All auxiliary components must still train on both outcome classes. This is a new local hypothesis, not a source-derived result. There is counterevidence against indiscriminate transfer: learned auxiliary transfer g3-r0006-learned_aux_transfer=0.6592574965, redistribution auxiliary transfer g3-r0012-redistrib_aux_live=0.6630471075, and live primary item geometry g3-r0021-aux_primary_live=0.6648664056 did not support broader auxiliary sharing in their respective matched lineages. Projection of position gradients in g3-r0017-position_gradient_project=0.6641686829 also failed to recover primary-only position quality (g3-r0017-position_gradient_primary=0.6655179496). Those null/negative trajectories remain evidence; they do not test this context/outcome boundary.

study.proposed_difference: Full 2x2: independent booleans context_positive_live and context_negative_live shared across the three auxiliary tasks. Forward creates a value-identical clone of shared context for each auxiliary tower and records those differentiable edges only for the immediately matching training loss; the primary uses the original context. No current labels are read in forward or retained for inference. The registered training_loss computes identical FP32 four mean BCEs in every cell with the declared fixed probability clamp. For auxiliary task t, Lblocked_t=mean(ell_t*(1-allowed(y_t))). Compute g_t=dLblocked_t/dc_t with torch.autograd.grad(retain_graph=True, create_graph=False), which does not accumulate parameter .grad values. Return Ltotal - sum_t <c_t-stop(c_t),stop(g_t)>. The subtracted value is exactly zero for finite states, its context derivative is g_t, and its tower derivative is zero. Therefore the final context derivative contains only allowed auxiliary loss sources, including cross-example Dice terms, while complete losses still update tower parameters and other paths. This is deliberate partial-gradient routing, not the ordinary gradient of an alternative class-weighted scalar objective. Every cell executes all three extra tower-to-context VJPs and clears ephemeral graph references. There are no new parameters or RNG draws. Source-only verification is available; torch is absent and no installation, training, data re-audit, model timing or scoring is authorized here. Host must check source digest, actual FeatureMap, numerical endpoints, BCE conventions, BF16 gradients and measured cost before a full trial. Prospective study and variant notes stage an evidence-linked scene-scoped record for host receipt/append-only memory handling. No human knowledge, past evidence or disabled personal memory is written. Reproduction is through each standalone Model module and its literal per-variant CONFIG, initialized from scratch by the authorized host with the unchanged protocol identified above. No local training command or new host CLI is invented.

falsifiers: Negative-only retains or exceeds the both-live benefit while positive-only matches neither: reject positive-dominant transfer for this implementation; negative losses or their optimization effect are the next candidate explanation.

Both-live equals or exceeds positive-only: no support for removing negative context derivatives as an improvement. Both isolated cells improve over neither and both-live improves further: evidence favors complementary contributions rather than the proposed interference.
No new cell exceeds both-live beyond paired-seed/user-cluster uncertainty: no supported new model improvement, even if one cell ranks first in this fixed seed. Remain preliminary without repetitions.

Any prediction/scalar-loss mismatch across cells at fixed state, material changes in tower/primary gradients, label access in forward, blocked-gradient leakage above BF16 tolerance, stale graph reuse, or nonfinite VJP invalidates mechanism attribution and requires repair before training.

Failure of historical endpoints after accounting for declared clamp/reduction conventions blocks cross-suite attribution; use only internally matched contrasts until resolved. All failed checks and partial runs still consume budget.

alternative_explanations: One fixed seed cannot establish robustness; all-enabled historical repeats are deterministic endpoint checks, not independent repetitions.
Changing context derivatives necessarily changes Adagrad accumulator trajectories and future tower inputs; no claim to isolate semantic complementarity from optimization or regularization.
Dense global clipping couples losses indirectly. Parameter gradients are preserved by the surrogate at a fixed state before clipping; subsequent learning trajectories can differ.

The fixed probability clamp is declared in the suite loss hook. Exact equality to the historical host default cannot be verified here; both/neither controls must be checked before cross-suite attribution.

Positive losses are naturally much rarer; unnormalized positive-only gradients have different magnitude. A positive-versus-negative contrast alone does not distinguish semantic content from gradient scale.
Computing partial VJPs through BF16 towers and subtracting blocked derivatives can leave rounding residuals; compare against explicit detached-context endpoint gradients and reject material leakage.

Auxiliary labels are 24h user/category/brand matches, not ad-specific conversion attribution. A positive-only effect could reflect that benchmark construction rather than a production intent mechanism.

Prior repeated endpoints share one seed and split and cannot establish independent replication; no data-level gradient alignment, causal feature validity, or local training prevalence was measured here.
